On 30 October 2024 the Council adopted UK draft S/2024/790 as resolution 2753 (2024) by 15–0–0. It renamed UNSOM as UNTMIS and began the transition on 1 November 2024. Phase one ran through 31 October 2025. The Council intended to end the mandate by 31 October 2026, subject to conditions on the ground. It requested two written Secretary-General reports before 30 March and 30 September 2025.

China: Welcomed adoption and called for Somali ownership and support tailored to national priorities. Urged transfer of knowledge and skills to local employees and wider local procurement.

Somalia: Welcomed adoption as implementing its own two-year handover request. Urged local procurement and hiring Somali staff, especially women, during drawdown.

United States: Voted yes and welcomed reviewing conditions before each transition phase. Objected to fewer Council reports and briefings.

China and Somalia both urged local procurement.

China emphasized Somali ownership. The US objected to reduced reporting.
